extracted.intended_audience: Anyone planning to submit an online math explainer to the Summer of Math Exposition (teachers, students, mathematicians, engineers, outreach creators) — prospective SoME entrants
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines and evaluation criteria for submitting a new math-focused explainer (video, blog post, interactive, etc.) to the Summer of Math Exposition contest. Covers eligibility constraints, required availability/language, and the judges' substantive criteria for selection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clarity
rubrics_metrics.description: Jargon should be explained, the goals of the lesson should be understandable with minimal background, and the submission should generally display empathy for people unfamiliar with the topic.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make the goals and terminology clear to learners; avoid unexplained jargon; demonstrate empathy for novices. This is an explicit top-level selection criterion used by judges.

rubrics_metrics.name: Motivation (first 30 seconds)
rubrics_metrics.description: It should be clear to the reader/viewer within the first 30 seconds why they should care.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Openings should quickly convey why the topic matters or why the viewer should continue watching/reading. This is an explicit timing expectation for judging initial engagement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Novelty
rubrics_metrics.description: It doesn't necessarily have to be an original idea or original topic, but it should offer someone an experience they might otherwise not have by searching around online.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Novelty can mean a better treatment of a common topic or surfacing an obscure idea. The submission should provide added value beyond existing online material.

rubrics_metrics.name: Memorability
rubrics_metrics.description: Something should make the piece easy to remember even several months later.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Memorable features might include beauty of presentation, presenter enthusiasm, or a striking 'aha' moment. Aim for hooks or presentation choices that stick with the audience.

rubrics_metrics.name: New work produced during the contest window
rubrics_metrics.description: It has to be something new you make this summer. It can't be something you already published before this contest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The spirit is to encourage new creators; reworking something previously published is discouraged unless it was only partially started and not published. Submissions must be created within the contest timeframe.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subject-matter: must be about math (broadly defined)
rubrics_metrics.description: It has to be about math. Here 'math' is meant very broadly; more applied topics like physics or computer science are abundantly welcome, as long as a viewer/reader might come away knowing something mathematical they didn't before.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the piece is primarily about a non-mathematical topic, it's not eligible; ensure the mathematical takeaway is clear.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specify assumed background level
rubrics_metrics.description: If you're assuming a certain background level for the target audience, kindly mention it below.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The judges may not have expertise in very niche areas (e.g., algebraic geometry), so clearly state required prerequisites; this helps set appropriate expectations and improves fairness in evaluation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accessibility for quick evaluation (5–10 minute visibility)
rubrics_metrics.description: For longer works, judges might not be able to consume the full video/post. The substance of your work should be clearly visible with a 5-10 minute view.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If your explainer is long (full lecture or long-form piece), structure it so core ideas/insights are evident early or provide a concise summary/preview so judges can assess value without consuming the entire work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Language requirement: English
rubrics_metrics.description: It has to be available in English. The judges here will be english speakers, so to be considered for the contest the lesson has to be accessible to them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: You may create content in other languages, but to be eligible for judging in this contest provide English-accessible material (subtitles, translation, or an English version).

rubrics_metrics.name: Publicly visible and free
rubrics_metrics.description: It has to be publicly visible and available for people to consume for free.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submissions behind paywalls, private links, or requiring payment are ineligible. Ensure the work is hosted where the public and judges can access it without cost.

rubrics_metrics.name: One entry per person or group
rubrics_metrics.description: One entry per person/group. We only have the capacity to judge participants based on a single entry.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you make multiple explainers, choose your best single submission for entry; teams should submit one entry per team.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allowed formats / mediums
rubrics_metrics.description: This is a competition where anyone can submit a video, blog post, interactive game, or whatever else they dream up.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The contest is format-agnostic: include videos, posts, interactive creations, games, etc. Focus on the explanatory value rather than conforming to a specific medium.

rubrics_metrics.name: Good-faith content / no offensive or irrelevant submissions
rubrics_metrics.description: This only applies to good faith submissions; anything irrelevant or offensive would not be included.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submissions should be sincere educational efforts; content that is intentionally irrelevant, malicious, or offensive will be excluded from consideration or the public lists.

rubrics_metrics.name: Peer-review prefilter and ranking procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: To be considered for the competition, we may ask you to peer review some of the other participants' submissions by looking at five other entries and ranking them 1-5 based on how well they fit the criteria above.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judging may involve participant peer review: you'll rank others, and those rankings will be aggregated (cumulative scoring) to pre-filter entries down to a few hundred for the judges. Be prepared to evaluate others according to the stated criteria.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selection process / judges' review
rubrics_metrics.description: A small group of judges will look through the entries with the criteria (Clarity, Motivation, Novelty, Memorable) in mind; depending on the number of entries, there may be a pre-filter step before final judgments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Understand that final winners are chosen by a small panel using the listed criteria; structure your submission to surface the strengths that align with those criteria for human reviewers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Target audience encouragement
rubrics_metrics.description: Who is this for? Anyone who might benefit others by sharing their knowledge (teachers, students, mathematicians, engineers, etc.). Entries from groups or teams are welcomed and encouraged too.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This clarifies inclusive intended audience and that group/team submissions are acceptable; craft your piece to benefit others and make clear who will gain from it.
